# Policy-KB bijection audit — medicare_supplement_policy_desk / task 0

Revision 1. Auditor: independent KB-doc auditor. Scanned against
`tasks/medicare_supplement_policy_desk/medigap.extended.yaml` (base `policies`, `parameter_schema`, `variants`,
`accounts`, `measures`, and the five `extended_policies` with their `overwrite`, `prerequisite`, `baseline`,
`factors`, `compute`, `compute_basis`), the five task-tool schemas as exposed at runtime, and the published
corpus `docs/medigap/*.json` (57 documents). The blind audit was frozen and hashed before any of this was
opened (`audits/runtime_context/medicare_supplement_policy_desk/_freeze_r1.txt`).

**Entry conditions (Step 0).** Policy-side verdict PASSED at round 2 — cited from the brief. `check_docs.py`
on `medigap` and `check_traceability.py` on this difficulty both green — output lines supplied with the brief and
reproduced in `_difficulty.md`; not re-run by the auditor. Runtime-visible view and a tool-shaped DB access path
were both supplied, and the DB side of the blind audit was genuinely blind (finder calls, never `initial_state`).
Nothing was missing from the input.

## source_to_kb

### Structural correspondence

| Source | Count | Documents | Role |

| `policies` | 11 | 11 | `policy` |
| `variants[].parameters` | 7 variants × 54 keys | 11 | `facet` |
| `extended_policies` | 5 | 5 hubs + 5 baselines | `hub`, `baseline` |

One-to-one, with no source object unhomed and no document without a source object. Mechanically checked: every
base policy id, every extended policy id and every one of the 25 `factors[].id` values resolves to exactly one
document; **every numeric and string value in every variant's `parameters` is rendered somewhere in the corpus**,
the single exception being the raw enum token `attained_age`, which is rendered as the business phrase
"attained age" (`premium_rating_schedule_2b4f2d9d`) — a required de-implementation, not an omission.

  discounted monthly premium together with the monthly share of the annual policy fee, that share being the

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the 57 documents was traced back. Results:

- **Additions of business steps: none.** The corpus contains no "please confirm the amount with the
  policyholder", no "review before handling", no "notify after completion", no "if it fails, follow some
  procedure". Every occurrence of the word *confirm* in the product is the phrase *"A confirmation sentence in
  plain text …"*, which is the tool's own return contract copied from the schema.
- **Cross-problem operational guidance: none.** No document tells the reader to handle another problem first,
  to call another problem's tool, or to route the case anywhere.
- **A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact: none.** Every illustration is introduced as
  hypothetical and uses figures that are not this world's. `premium_account_settlement_computation_2871445e`
  works through a Plan N policy **billed monthly** at 114.71 with a single charge and no payment at all;
  Marguerite's policy is Plan N billed quarterly at 452.82 with five charges, four payments and a refund.
  `overlap_premium_return_computation_7d397a4b` works through a charge of 151.30 covering one month; her opening
  span carries 452.82 over three. No document states that any customer has arrears, a missing bill or an
  overlapping enrollment.
- **Pointers between documents: none.** Mechanically checked for "as set out in", "see the", "refer to",
  "described elsewhere", "unless otherwise", "except as", "subject to any" — zero hits in the product.
- **Tier-telling: none.** No factor document says which tier a customer or most customers fall on, and none
  describes the reading a person without the rule would take as a mistake to avoid.
- **One class of sentence is sourced but sits in the wrong document.** Five computation documents carry a topic
  sentence drawn from the extended policy's full `rule` rather than from its `baseline.rule`. Each has a
  structured source, so this is not a claim from outside the source and not a reverse-scan addition; it is a
  discrete-topology failure and is recorded once, in full, under `dependency_form` below.

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION PASS.**

Every normative atom of the structured source is entailed by the published documents; nothing is unborne,
nothing is borne with changed meaning, and no claim from outside the source appears. The single `overwrite` is
written as retired and nothing else is. The `prerequisite` is carried verbatim, in its declared form, on the
blocked side and nowhere else. Every one of the 25 declared factors has its own document carrying its whole
ladder, every tier exact. No previous revision exists for this difficulty; this is revision 1.

### Policy-side notes (reported, not counted against this verdict)

These originate on the policy side — the source's own prose does not fully determine its own `compute` — and the
documents render that prose faithfully. Recorded here per Step 4, and they do not change the verdict.

**PS-1 — the current billing period's charge can be counted twice.** The renderer raised this as a lead; it is
real, and it is in the source. `result` is
`MX(0.0, RND(current_span_value + arrears_charges + fee_instalment - credits_allowed - returns_credited, 2))`,
where `current_span_value` is the charge posted for the current period whenever one stands, and `arrears_charges`
sums every charge posted inside `arrears_window_months`. The current period lies inside that window on **every**
tier, not only on the fall-through — so whenever a charge stands for the current period it is added twice. The
fall-through (`arrears_window_months = span_months`) is merely the sharpest case, where the two terms are exactly
equal. The published document states this and its worked example demonstrates it:
*"The billing period now current is valued at the amount posted for it, being 114.71. The settlement reaches back
over that period alone, and the charges posted within it come to 114.71. … Adding 114.71, 114.71 and 1.67 gives
231.09"* (`premium_account_settlement_computation_2871445e`).

**Does it bear on this task's scored solution? No — it is latent, on two independent counts.**
(i) The gold path does not take the fall-through: `months_in_force` = 15 (effective 2025-06-01, frozen
2026-09-21) and `settling_payments_in_year` = 2 (the payments of 2025-12-02 and 2026-03-03), so
`arrears_window_months = K('extended_arrears_window_months') = 12` — tier 1 of `arrears_reach`.
(ii) More decisively, no charge at all stands for the current billing period: the ledger's last charges were
posted 2026-06-01, outside `within_months = span_months = 3`, so `current_span_charges = 0` and
`current_span_value` comes from the rate (452.82), disjoint from `arrears_charges`. **Nothing is counted twice
on this path.** Had a charge of 452.82 been posted for 2026-09, the settlement would have come out 452.82 too
high. So: a latent defect in an untaken branch, not a source-layer miss bearing on this task — the step 2 loop
does not need to be reopened on this account.

**PS-2 — the issue-age step's prose does not determine its compute.** The source pins
`age_rated_monthly_premium = RND(P('base_monthly_premium_age_65') * (1 + P('issue_age_rate_step_percent')/100 *
issue_age_steps), 2)` — a **flat** multiple, **rounded to the cent at that step**. Its own ladder text says only
*"the base monthly premium rises by the tier's issue-age step for each year of age above 65"*, and
`parameter_schema.issue_age_rate_step_percent` only *"Percentage the base premium rises for each year of issue
age above 65."* Neither compounding nor the intermediate rounding is fixed anywhere in prose, and
`age_rating_of_the_monthly_premium_cb51280c`'s illustration stops before the arithmetic: *"the base monthly
premium of 164.20 rises by the plan letter's issue-age step of 2.8 per cent for each of those 3 years"*, with no
resulting figure. On this task the three readings give 452.82 (flat, rounded at the step — the source's),
452.85 (flat, rounded once) and 463.08 (compound), carrying the settlement to 530.21, 530.24 and 540.47. The
document is a faithful carriage of the source's own text, so this is not a rendering defect; but a solver has to
anchor on the four historical quarterly charges of 452.82 to exclude the other two readings, as this audit's
blind derivation did. The gap is between the source's prose and the source's compute, which no gate inspects.

**PS-3 — the bank-transfer reduction is described on two different bases.**
`parameter_schema.electronic_funds_transfer_discount` reads *"Flat reduction each **billing period** for paying
by bank transfer"*, rendered verbatim in `premium_discount_schedule_f9b6c632` (*"a flat amount taken each billing
period"*), while the factor's ladder tier says *"for each **month** of the span"* and the compute applies it per
month. Both wordings are the source's, and the corpus renders both. It is determinate at the point of use —
`value_of_the_current_billing_period_a10d72d1` shows *"114.71 less 2.00, being 112.71, taken for each of the 3
months the cadence covers, giving 338.13"* — so a solver who reads the governing documents is not misled; but the
schedule document, read alone, states a different basis, and the difference here would be 4.00 on the settlement.

## dependency_form

### KB-EXPLICIT RED — the computation documents announce that a variation exists

**Symptom.** Four of the five computation documents (role `baseline`) assert, in the same breath as the standard
method, that the quantity the standard method sets to nothing is in fact taken, added or only partly applied.
A reader of the computation document alone is thereby told that something outside it decides that quantity —
which is exactly what the corpus must not say: the existence of a factor is to be discovered from the customer's
records, not announced by the baseline.

**Root cause.** The source draws a clean line: `extended_policies[].rule` contains the topic sentence *and* the
variations; `extended_policies[].baseline.rule` contains the standard method only and deliberately omits those
topic sentences. The rendering has taken the topic sentences from the full `rule` into the baseline document.
Mechanically confirmed by diffing each computation document's sentences against its `baseline.rule`.

**Evidence — the five places, each with its document and the sentence it sits beside.**

1. `crossover_benefit_settlement_computation_cae09cc7`, section *"4. The yearly deductible"*:
   > *"A yearly deductible is taken from that amount before the share is worked out. No yearly deductible is
   > taken, the benefit carrying none."*
   The first sentence is in `rule` but not in `baseline.rule`. It tells the reader a yearly deductible exists on
   some path — which is the whole content of the factor `travel_deductible_taken`.

2. `premium_account_settlement_computation_2871445e`, section *"2. The monthly premium the policy is rated on"*:
   > *"A reduction is then taken for the way the policyholder pays from the monthly premium the household
   > discount leaves, so that the household discount and the reduction for the way they pay are taken one after
   > the other and are never combined into a single rate. No reduction is taken from that monthly premium."*
   In `rule`, not in `baseline.rule`. It announces the factor `payment_method_reduction` — **which is a factor
   this task's scored figure turns on** (the 2.00 per month that makes the current period 452.82 rather than
   458.82).

3. `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`, section *"Which of them are restated"*:
   > *"Only some of those lines are restated here. Every line that falls outside cover is restated."*
   In `rule`, not in `baseline.rule`. "Only some" against "every" in consecutive sentences can only be
   reconciled by a rule the reader is being told lives elsewhere — the factor `lines_restated_here`.

4. `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`, section *"What stays with the policyholder"*:
   > *"Part of that liability is not restated, because the coverage that was in force on those days leaves the
   > policyholder something of its own. The policyholder is left nothing, and the whole of the liability is
   > restated."*
   In `rule`, not in `baseline.rule`. Same shape, and it goes further: it states the *reason* a variation exists
   ("because the coverage that was in force on those days leaves the policyholder something of its own"), which
   is the trigger of the factor `other_coverage_retention`.

5. `overlap_premium_return_computation_7d397a4b`, section *"4. What is returned with the premium"*:
   > *"Alongside the premium itself the plan returns the other rate components posted for the opening span, month
   > by month. The premium alone is returned, and nothing is added for any other rate component."*
   In `rule`, not in `baseline.rule`. It announces the factor `returned_rate_components` — **also a factor this
   task's scored figure turns on** (the 1.67 per month that makes the return 145.43 rather than 143.76).

**Affected documents and locations.** `crossover_benefit_settlement_computation_cae09cc7` §4;
`premium_account_settlement_computation_2871445e` §2;
`precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e` §§ "Which of them are restated", "What stays with the
policyholder"; `overlap_premium_return_computation_7d397a4b` §4.
`direct_benefit_repayment_computation_0cd18862` is clean on this point — its topic sentences
(*"The overpayment on those lines is then measured."*, *"What has already come back from others is then set
against it."*, *"The balance those lines record standing to the policyholder's credit is set against it as
well."*) name the quantity without asserting that anything varies.

**Borderline, recorded but not counted RED.** `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`:
*"What is left with the policyholder falls across the lines outside cover. It is not applied at all, no line
falling outside cover."* — the second clause explains the first away on the baseline's own facts, so it does not
by itself announce a variation. Listed for completeness.

### Everything else in the dependency-form scan: clean

- **No state-form sentence restated as an action.** The prerequisite sentence and its restatement in
  `premium_account_settlement_desk_basis_9675c938` both name the state (*"the premium account carries the return
  owed…"*, *"Until such a return stands on that account"*). Neither names a performer, an action, a policy or a
  document. Same-form restatement in the same document is the source's own form and is not a finding.
- **No other problem's tool name anywhere.** Mechanically checked: each of the five task tool names occurs in
  exactly one document — its own policy's hub, inside that hub's own invocation block — and none of the 27 task
  tool names belonging to the other five products occurs at all.
- **No dependency stated in a second document.** Each of the three `policy_source` sentences occurs in exactly
  one of the 57 documents.
- **No aggregated chain.** No document carries a dependency table, a checklist, a roadmap, a complete route or
  an ordered list stringing problems together. No FAQ or example walks across problems.
- **No cross-problem operational guidance.** Nothing of the form "if unmet, first call …" or "handle X before Y"
  beyond the prerequisite sentences themselves.
- **No wrong-versus-right contrast and no named mistake** anywhere in the product.
- **Titles name general subjects.** *"Settlement of a Medicare Supplement Premium Account in Arrears"* and
  *"Returning Supplement Premium Charged for Days Covered by Another Medicare Coverage"* name the request type
  and the correction type each policy is defined by, not a caller's situation. No title or opening restates a
  customer request or labels a procedure for a specific case.
- **Findability without borrowed phrasing.** The depended-on hub is reachable through the words the records and
  the sentence use — "return", "premium charged", "Medicare Advantage enrollment … still in force" — not only
  through the blocked document's wording.

**Verdict: KB-EXPLICIT RED**, on the five statements listed above. The semantics they carry is "a variation of
this quantity exists"; the solution remains unique and correct, and the runtime and bijection parts both pass.

`baseline.rule` and against its full `rule` — on the current corpus, rather than accepting the renderer's
account. All five are gone, and each section now states the standard method alone:

| 2 | `premium_account_settlement_computation_2871445e` §2: *"A reduction is then taken for the way the policyholder pays…"* | **the paragraph in full:** *"No reduction is taken from that monthly premium."* — closed |
| 3 | `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`: *"Only some of those lines are restated here."* | ***"**Which of them are restated.** Every line that falls outside cover is restated."* — closed |
| 4 | same document: *"Part of that liability is not restated, because the coverage that was in force on those days leaves the policyholder something of its own."* | ***"**What stays with the policyholder.** The policyholder is left nothing, and the whole of the liability is restated."* — closed |
| 5 | `overlap_premium_return_computation_7d397a4b` §4: *"Alongside the premium itself the plan returns the other rate components posted for the opening span, month by month."* | **§4 in full:** *"The premium alone is returned, and nothing is added for any other rate component."* — closed |

The three the renderer found itself are likewise gone, and I confirm all three were real:

- `premium_account_settlement_computation_2871445e` §4 — *"The settlement then reaches back over the periods
  still standing on the account"* removed and the heading changed from "The periods reached back over" to
  **"The span reached back over"**. The sentence was in `rule`, not in `baseline.rule`, and "the periods still
  standing" (plural) sat against a standard method reaching over "the billing period now current alone"
  (singular) — the plural was itself the announcement that a wider span exists. Real, and correctly removed.
- `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e` — *"What is left with the policyholder falls across the
  lines outside cover"* removed, heading now **"Applying what is left with the policyholder"**. In `rule`, not
  in `baseline.rule`; "falls across the lines" announced a spreading rule the standard method does not apply.
  Real.
- same document — *"Money already taken back is never taken back twice"* removed. **Question 3, tested and the
  renderer's reading confirmed by the source itself:** the sentence is in
  `medigap_ext_uncovered_day_line_restatement.rule` and **not** in that policy's `baseline.rule`, while the
  parallel principle *"Money the plan has already given back is never given back twice"* **is** a sentence of
  `medigap_ext_dual_coverage_premium_return.baseline.rule`. So the source does draw exactly the distinction the
  renderer relied on: the principle is baseline content for the return policy and deliberately not baseline
  content for the restatement policy. Consistently, the sentence is **kept** in
  `overlap_premium_return_computation_7d397a4b` §5 and **removed** from the restatement document. Nothing the
  source carries was dropped.

## Question 1 — is the criterion right, and do the kept sentences stay on the naming side?

The renderer's criterion: *a topic sentence may name a quantity, but must not assert it is taken, added or
restricted, nor state why a variation exists.*

**The criterion is right, and it is not merely inferred from my clean document — it is forced by the source.**
I tested it against `baseline.rule` itself, and six mandatory baseline sentences have exactly the shape "name a
quantity that the standard method then sets to nothing", for example:

> `medigap_ext_uncovered_day_line_restatement.baseline.rule`: *"What is restated is the recorded liability of the
> lines that fall outside cover, **less what the coverage that was in force on those days leaves the
> policyholder** and less what has already been taken back"* — in the same baseline as *"The standard method
> leaves the policyholder nothing."*

A criterion that banned naming a quantity the standard method zeroes would make the baseline uncarriable, and
dropping it would be a RED in the opposite direction. The only coherent line is the one drawn: what must not
appear is **the same predicate affirmed and then denied** ("a yearly deductible **is taken**" / "**no** yearly
deductible is taken"; "**only some**" / "**every**"; "part **is not** restated" / "the **whole** is restated"),
and **any statement of why a variation exists** (RED 4's "because the coverage that was in force on those days
leaves the policyholder something of its own"). Every one of the eight removals falls on that side, and none of
the seven retentions does.

**The seven kept sentences, each judged against the failure mode.** My matcher enumerates six directly and
absorbs the seventh into the adjacent baseline sentence; listing all seven:

| Document | Kept sentence | Beside it | Judgement |
|---|---|---|---|
| settlement §3 | *"The premium owed for the billing period now current is then fixed."* | *"That period is valued at the amount posted for it."* | pure sequencing; no predicate affirmed then denied — **naming side** |
| settlement §6 | *"Money already received is then set against what is owed."* | *"The payments that settled a billing period in full … are credited."* | the baseline does credit something; no contradiction — **naming side** |
| precoverage | *"The liability of the lines restated is measured from the record."* | *"Nothing is taken as the liability of those lines."* | names where the measure comes from; "measured from the record" is not denied by "nothing is taken" (a zero measure is still measured) — **naming side** |
| repayment | *"The overpayment on those lines is then measured."* | *"Nothing is found overpaid."* | sequencing — **naming side** (unchanged document; this is my round-1 clean reference) |
| repayment | *"What has already come back from others is then set against it."* | *"Nothing is set against it."* | names the term of the formula; a zero term is still a term — **naming side** |
| repayment | *"The balance those lines record standing to the policyholder's credit is set against it as well."* | *"She is credited with nothing."* | same shape — **naming side** |
| crossover §5 | *"What counts toward that deductible is measured from the claim record: the liability the paid lines of the twelve months to date record is what counts."* | — | names the source of the measure and then states the standard method in the same sentence; no entry, restatement or recovery is mentioned — **naming side** |

**No kept sentence announces a variation.** None says a quantity is taken, added or restricted where the
standard method zeroes it; none says which customers differ; none gives a reason a variation exists; none names
another document, factor, tool or policy. The count discrepancy between my enumeration and the renderer's
(6 + 1 absorbed vs 7; 14 vs 15 originally) is a sentence-splitting artefact around the bolded run-in headings
and is immaterial — I enumerated and judged every remaining import myself.
